text:
Andrew Copp is playing more than 18 minutes a night for Detroit and has six points in 18 games to show for it. Our numbers think that undersells him, though not by as much as you might hope.

The bad luck is mostly around him. The Red Wings have scored 5.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him assists, and that usually swings back. He is shooting 6.9% on 3.8 expected goals. But Detroit also gets outplayed at 5-on-5 with him on, 49% of expected goals and six points worse than without him, so not all of it is luck.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 8.5 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 85th percentile among forwards, and leaving the zone with the puck on 62% of his exits. Evolving-Hockey noted his 2025-26 results ran well ahead of his chances, which makes this year look like the other side of that coin. Our range has him at 32 to 52 points.
headline: Copp is due for some help from his linemates
